title: Critical bifurcation and deconfined quantum criticality in an interacting cluster Ising chain
authors: Sourabh, Bachana Beradze, Mikheil Tsitsishvili, Alexander Nersesyan, Titas Chanda
abstract: We investigate the cluster Ising chain with an additional nearest-neighbor interaction using tensor-network methods and a weak-coupling field theory. Without the interaction, the Jordan-Wigner transformation decomposes the model into a triplet of identical Majorana chains related by an exact $O(3)$ flavor symmetry. Their common mass vanishes at the $SU(2)_2$ Wess-Zumino-Novikov-Witten critical point with central charge $c = 3/2$ separating the symmetry-protected topological cluster phase from a ferromagnet. The interaction reduces $O(3)$ to its cyclic subgroup $C_3$, splitting the triplet into a singlet and a doublet whose gaps close separately, producing a critical bifurcation into Ising ($c = 1/2$) and Gaussian ($c = 1$) critical lines. A second ferromagnetic phase opens between these critical lines for repulsive interactions and a disordered phase for attractive ones. The Gaussian line then separates two Landau-incompatible ferromagnets, realizing a deconfined quantum critical line with emergent $O(2)$ symmetry, along which our independently extracted exponents vary continuously yet satisfy the parameter-free relation $β= (2ν- 1)/4$ of the eight-vertex weak universality class. At stronger repulsion this line opens into an extended gapless floating phase with incommensurate algebraic correlations, entered through Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. All of these phases and the transitions between them are captured by the weak-coupling theory. Beyond its regime of validity, our simulations reveal a translation-symmetry-breaking antiferromagnet reached through first-order transitions.
summary: This work analyzes the quantum phase transitions in an interacting cluster Ising chain, demonstrating how a weak interaction causes a critical bifurcation from an initial high-symmetry critical point. The study successfully maps out a deconfined quantum critical line characterized by emergent O(2) symmetry, using a combination of tensor-network methods and weak-coupling field theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates the critical bifurcation and the nature of deconfined quantum criticality (DQC) in an interacting cluster Ising chain.
main_result: The interaction splits the non-interacting critical point into two distinct critical lines (Ising and Gaussian), leading to a DQC line with emergent O(2) symmetry, which is captured by weak-coupling field theory.
method: The study employs tensor-network methods and weak-coupling field theory, supplemented by numerical simulations (MPS) to analyze the phase diagram.
model_or_system: The system is the cluster Ising chain (CIM) augmented with a nearest-neighbor interaction. The non-interacting limit exhibits an O(3) symmetry and a critical point at c=3/2.
key_observables: Bipartite entanglement entropy (S), string order parameter (OS), and magnetizations in x, y, and z directions.
important_parameters: The interaction strength ($V_{	ext{nn}}$) and the coupling constants ($\lambda$) are key parameters controlling the phase transitions.
main_assumptions: The weak-coupling theory is assumed valid in the analyzed regimes, though simulations reveal first-order transitions beyond its scope.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the critical bifurcation, showing the splitting of the initial critical point into Ising (c=1/2) and Gaussian (c=1) lines, and mapping out the subsequent DQC line and floating phase.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the non-interacting limit (O(3) symmetry, c=3/2), then introduces the interaction which causes a critical bifurcation into two separate critical lines. It then analyzes the DQC line connecting two ferromagnets and the subsequent floating phase, concluding with the failure of the theory at strong coupling.
why_interesting: The detailed mapping of quantum phase transitions, especially the realization of DQC and the connection to specific universality classes (like the eight-vertex model), provides deep insights into strongly correlated quantum matter.
